original: b.	Landlord Termination Right. Landlord may terminate this Lease by written notice given within sixty (60) days after a casualty if: (i) Landlord's contractor estimates that restoration will take more than two hundred seventy (270) days from the date of the casualty; (ii) the casualty occurs during the final twenty-four (24) months of the Term; (iii) insurance proceeds are insufficient to fund restoration; or (iv) Landlord's mortgagee applies the proceeds in reduction of the loan.
revised: b.	Landlord Termination Right. Landlord may terminate this Lease by written notice given within sixty (60) days after a casualty if: (i) Landlord's contractor estimates that restoration will take more than one hundred eighty (180) days from the date of the casualty; (ii) the casualty occurs during the final eighteen (18) months of the Term; or (iii) Landlord's mortgagee applies the proceeds in reduction of the loan. If Landlord exercises the termination right hereunder, Landlord may not re-let the Premises to another tenant within twelve (12) months of the termination without first re-offering them to Larkfield.

original: Section 2.  Restricted Activities.  Tenant shall not, without Landlord’s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld: (a) provide overnight inpatient care or overnight boarding of patients at the Leased Premises; (b) store, use, or dispose of Hazardous Materials at the Leased Premises other than in types and quantities customary for, and in compliance with applicable law governing, outpatient medical and diagnostic practices of the kind Tenant operates, including routine clinical, laboratory, and pharmaceutical materials; or (c) conduct any activity that would void or materially increase the cost of Landlord’s building insurance, provided Landlord shall first notify Tenant of any such increased cost and afford Tenant a reasonable opportunity to cease the activity giving rise to it before treating the same as a default.
revised: Section 2.  Restricted Activities; Hazardous Materials.  Tenant shall not conduct any activity that would void or materially increase the cost of Landlord’s insurance or exceed the floor-load, electrical, plumbing, water, exhaust, parking, or other capacity allocated to the Leased Premises, or cause vibration, odor, noise, or radiofrequency interference affecting other tenants. “Hazardous Materials” includes regulated medical waste, sharps, pathological and pharmaceutical waste, chemotherapeutic and hazardous drugs, radiologic and nuclear materials, fixatives, sterilant gases, and controlled substances. Tenant may use customary quantities necessary for the Permitted Use only in compliance with law, using licensed vendors, and shall not store any such materials in common areas or shared refuse facilities. Tenant shall maintain manifests, disposal records, its OSHA exposure-control plan, hazard-communication program, and sharps-injury log and shall provide redacted copies to Landlord upon reasonable request.

original: Section 2.  Renewal Term Rent. revised: Section 2.  Renewal Term Rent.
